newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends sharply down on stop-loss sales.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends sharply down on stop-loss sales.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures contract closed sharply lower on Friday as stop-loss selling accelerated after it broke below a key support point of 99.00.

After Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan signalled on Thursday that U.S. rates may be raised as early as next week, speculative sales hit the contract and this prompted further unwinding of long positions which initially started on Tuesday.

Traders said many dealers started unwinding longs on Tuesday when the finance minister said the government's land measures will be announced on March 31, and remarks by a BOJ senior official implied that the long-term bond market had overshot. The TIFEE was closed for a holiday on Thursday.

"The contract's fall below 99.00 means that the market has factored in an end of the BOJ's current guidance of the key overnight call rate below 0.50 percent," said a dealer at a major brokerage house.
The December fell as low as 98.89, the lowest for any benchmark since August 7, 1996.
It settled at 98.90 on turnover of 146,119 contracts.
There were vague rumours Japan's industrial output forecast for April, due on March 28, may be better than expected.
Another factor weighing on Euroyen futures was the recent upward momentum in cash Euroyen interest rates ahead of the fiscal year-end, traders said.

Selling on the December may stop at 98.87 before it falls to 98.70, traders said. But a long-term credit bank dealer said the December may nosedive if the Nikkei stock index rises to or above 19,500 because there is a belief that Japanese interest rates will not be raised unless the Nikkei rises to 20,000.
The BOJ maintained a neutral operation this morning.

But the key overnight call rate jumped to 0.53 percent from Wednesday's weighted average of 0.51 percent. The long-end benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rate also rose to 0.58 percent, its highest since August 23, 1996.

Many investors were hesitant to supply one- to two-week funds to the money market as the book closings approach, while strong bank demand continued for funds covering the fiscal year-end on March 31. This resulted in upward momentum in short-term interest rates across the board, traders said. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-33432-8570
